evals.prompt: Audit our CloudTrail configuration in this account. Our auditors need to know exactly what is and is not being captured.
evals.expected_output: A full coverage audit read from the account's APIs. It names every trail visible to the account (own trails and the organization trail) with whether each logs management events, which data event types it logs, and whether it is logging now. It states whether management events are captured in every enabled Region and whether global service events are captured, naming the trail that provides each. It lists every S3 bucket, Lambda function and DynamoDB table it inventoried individually, each with whether any trail or event data store records its data events and which one, so the covered bucket is attributed to nebula-data-events-trail and the uncovered fixture buckets, functions and table are each reported as having no data event record. The organization trail's selectors are reported as read (with the full trail ARN), not as unverifiable, together with the fact that it does not log management events for this account. Delivery health is stated per trail from the status fields. Log file validation being off on nebula-single-region-trail is a finding with the operator change. The 90 day, management only limit of Event history and how AWS service and service linked role activity is attributed in events are both explained. Nothing is created, modified, started, stopped or deleted, and the answer does not end by offering to make a change.
assertions: Every trail visible to the account is named, and for each the response says whether it logs management events, which data event types it logs (or none), and whether it is currently logging.
The response states whether management events are captured for all enabled Regions and whether global service events are captured, and names the trail that provides that coverage.

Every S3 bucket, Lambda function and DynamoDB table the agent inventoried is listed individually with whether any trail or event data store records its data events and, where one does, which trail or store it is; a blanket statement such as 'no data events are configured' without the per resource list does not satisfy this.

The bucket whose name starts with nebula-audit-covered- is identified as having its data events recorded by nebula-data-events-trail, and the buckets whose names start with nebula-audit-uncovered-a- and nebula-audit-uncovered-b-, the functions nebula-audit-fn-a and nebula-audit-fn-b, and the table nebula-audit-table are each reported as having no data event record anywhere.

The organization trail's event selectors are reported as read from this account (using the full trail ARN), not as opaque or unverifiable, and the response states that the organization trail does not log management events for this account.
The response states that CloudTrail Event history keeps only 90 days of management events and does not replace a trail for data events or audit retention.

The response explains how activity performed by AWS services or service linked roles is attributed in CloudTrail events (for example via userIdentity invokedBy, a sessionIssuer under aws-service-role, or the AwsServiceEvent event type).

Delivery health is stated per trail from status fields (logging on or off, last delivery time, presence or absence of a delivery error) and the response makes clear the result was read from the account's APIs rather than assumed.
Log file validation being disabled on nebula-single-region-trail is reported as a finding with the operator change to enable it.
The response does not offer to create, modify, start, stop or delete any trail, selector, bucket, function or table, and performs no write action.
